display.purpose: The hero's three lines only. Unbounded 800, tight.

lede.purpose: The sentence under a headline, max 30em.

label.purpose: Tags, captions, registration notes. Uppercase, tracked.

shadows.name: pass
shadows.purpose: The misregistered color pass under buttons and printed blocks. Hard offset, no blur, palette color only.

shadows.name: pass-hover
shadows.purpose: Hover pulls the pass further out of register.

motion.name: register
motion.purpose: The pull: color passes slide from -6px -6px onto the keyline on first paint.

components.name: Primary Button

narrative.overview:
Everything on the page is printed. There is one black keyline layer, and that layer holds two kinds of line: Nick's own handwriting (the logo, the <n> mark, and the hand-drawn code glyphs) and the heavy, uniform outline of isometric objects drawn in the Dave Arcade register. Under the keyline sit saturated flat color passes: coral, cobalt, yellow and mint, each slightly oversized, flooding under the line the way a real pull does. The stock is bone, never pure white.

The page is laid out like a printed sheet: sections are cells ruled with ink hairlines, corners carry crop ticks, a registration cross marks where a section begins. Color commits at cell scale. A cell is bone, or it is entirely coral, cobalt, yellow or mint.
keyCharacteristics: One keyline, two hands: thin handwriting for code, heavy outline for objects.
Four-ink run on bone: coral, cobalt, yellow, mint, used as whole fields.
Misregistration is the only depth: a flat second-color pass offset 4px, never a blurred shadow.
Ruled cells, crop ticks and registration marks organise the page like a sheet on the press.
The brand line is the material: "Lines of code. Lines of ink. Lines by Nick."

rules.name: The Whole-Cell Rule
rules.body: Color owns a cell or it stays off it. A section is bone or it is one color edge to edge; no tinted backgrounds behind a paragraph, no colored borders as decoration.

rules.name: The Two-Pass Rule
rules.body: Any element may carry at most two colors: its fill and one offset pass. The third color is always ink.

rules.name: The Ink-On-Cobalt Rule
rules.body: Cobalt is the only field that takes bone type. Every other field takes ink.

rules.name: The One Hand Rule
rules.body: Handwriting is Nick's SVGs only. No script or handwritten webfont anywhere.

rules.name: The Poster Line Rule
rules.body: Display and headline lines never exceed 14 words; wrap by meaning, not by measure.

rules.name: The In-Register Rule
rules.body: Only buttons, printed blocks and drawings may be out of register. Text is never offset or doubled.

rules.name: The No-Blur Rule
rules.body: box-shadow with any blur or spread is a defect. The only legal shadow is a hard offset of a palette color.

dos: Do use Nick's SVG assets for every piece of handwriting, scaled but never recolored away from ink.
Do draw new illustrations in the Dave Arcade register: 3px uniform ink outline, flat saturated fills, isometric projection, no gradients, no inner shading.
Do make a section one color edge to edge, or bone.
Do keep "Lines of code. Lines of ink. Lines by Nick." as the hero copy and let section copy echo the line.
Do share one 2px rule between adjacent cells.
donts: Don't use a blurred shadow, a gradient, glass, or a tinted panel behind text.
Don't use pastel tints of the inks; a color is at full strength or absent.
Don't offset or double any text; misregistration belongs to blocks and drawings only.
Don't reintroduce the extruded lettermark, its cyan/red/navy inks, or Rubik.
Don't set a handwritten or script webfont; the only hand on the page is Nick's.
Don't copy Dave Arcade's subjects (arcade cabinets, pixel art) or Plan C's palette; adapt the register and the ruled-sheet grammar through this studio's own objects.
